questions.prompt: The bulk movement of air into and out of lungs is called _____.
questions.hint: Think about moving air, not exchanging molecules across a membrane.
questions.explanation: Ventilation depends on pressure gradients created by thoracic muscle activity.

questions.prompt: The respiratory system contributes to blood _____ by regulating CO₂ exhalation.
questions.hint: Consider the concentration of hydrogen ions.
questions.explanation: CO₂ shifts the CO₂/HCO₃⁻ equilibrium and can change acidity.

questions.prompt: The region ending at terminal bronchioles is the _____ portion of the respiratory tract.
questions.hint: No direct alveolar exchange occurs in this portion.
questions.explanation: The conducting zone transports and conditions air; alveoli appear farther downstream.

questions.prompt: The exchange of gases between systemic capillaries and tissue cells is _____ respiration.
questions.hint: This occurs away from the lungs in body tissues.
questions.explanation: Internal respiration refers to systemic gas exchange, distinct from cellular ATP production.

questions.prompt: The posterior openings of the nasal cavities into the nasopharynx are the _____.
questions.hint: They are sometimes called the internal nostrils.
questions.explanation: Choanae connect the nasal cavity and nasopharynx.

questions.prompt: The curved folds that increase airflow turbulence in the nose are nasal _____.
questions.hint: There are superior, middle, and inferior ones.
questions.explanation: Conchae increase airflow contact with respiratory mucosa.

questions.prompt: The passageway immediately below a nasal concha is a nasal _____.
questions.hint: A three-part series of air passages accompanies the conchae.
questions.explanation: A meatus is the airway space beneath a concha.

questions.prompt: The nasal hair structures that intercept larger airborne particles are _____.
questions.hint: They are coarse hairs near the entrance to the nose.
questions.explanation: Vibrissae help trap larger particulates before they reach smaller passages.

questions.prompt: The upper pharyngeal region lying behind the nasal cavity is the _____.
questions.hint: It begins above the soft palate.
questions.explanation: The nasopharynx primarily conducts air.

questions.prompt: The beating cilia that move mucus toward the pharynx are part of the mucociliary _____.
questions.hint: Also called the mucus escalator.
questions.explanation: Ciliary transport removes trapped particles and microbes.

questions.prompt: The connective-tissue layer beneath the airway epithelium is the _____.
questions.hint: It supports epithelial cells, vessels, and immune components.
questions.explanation: The lamina propria is part of the mucosa.

questions.prompt: Much of the trachea is lined by _____ ciliated columnar epithelium.
questions.hint: Nuclei appear at different heights despite cells contacting the basement membrane.
questions.explanation: This specialized epithelium often includes goblet cells.

questions.prompt: The one-cell-thick, flattened epithelial lining most suited for alveolar diffusion is simple _____.
questions.hint: Thin flat cells minimize diffusion distance.
questions.explanation: Type I pneumocytes are squamous cells.

questions.prompt: The mucus-producing epithelial cells common in larger conducting airways are _____ cells.
questions.hint: Named after their cup-like shape.
questions.explanation: Goblet cells secrete airway mucus.

questions.prompt: The true vocal cords are the vocal _____.
questions.hint: Contrast them with the false vocal cords.
questions.explanation: True vocal folds vibrate during phonation.

questions.prompt: The false vocal cords are the _____ folds.
questions.hint: These folds lie superior to the true folds.
questions.explanation: Vestibular folds contribute to airway protection.

questions.prompt: The unpaired laryngeal cartilage forming a complete ring is the _____.
questions.hint: It lies inferior to the thyroid cartilage.
questions.explanation: Cricoid forms a ring just above the first tracheal ring.

questions.prompt: Production of voice by vibrating the vocal folds is called _____.
questions.hint: Not the same as shaping speech with lips and tongue.
questions.explanation: Phonation is vocal sound production; articulation shapes it into speech.

questions.prompt: The paired cartilages that directly adjust vocal-fold positions are the _____.
questions.hint: These move like small levers at the posterior glottis.
questions.explanation: Arytenoid motion regulates the opening and closing of the glottis.

questions.prompt: The posterior smooth muscle spanning the C-shaped tracheal cartilage rings is the _____.
questions.hint: Its name resembles the airway in which it sits.
questions.explanation: This muscle changes tracheal diameter and accommodates posterior flexibility.

questions.prompt: The tracheal bifurcation contains a prominent internal ridge called the _____.
questions.hint: Often triggers a cough when contacted.
questions.explanation: Carina marks division of the main bronchi.

questions.prompt: A bronchus delivering air to a single lung lobe is a _____ bronchus.
questions.hint: Think of the airway hierarchy primary → secondary → tertiary.
questions.explanation: Secondary/lobar bronchi supply lung lobes.

questions.prompt: The last conducting airways before alveoli begin to appear are _____ bronchioles.
questions.hint: Their successors are respiratory bronchioles.
questions.explanation: Terminal bronchioles end the conducting zone.

questions.prompt: Unlike bronchi, bronchioles contain no supporting _____.
questions.hint: Smooth muscle becomes important for airway diameter.
questions.explanation: Bronchioles lack cartilage, unlike the larger bronchi.

questions.prompt: The typical right lung contains _____ lobes.
questions.hint: More than the left lung.
questions.explanation: The right lung has superior, middle, and inferior lobes.

questions.prompt: The usual left lung is separated by the _____ fissure.
questions.hint: Both lungs have this fissure, but only the right typically has a horizontal one.
questions.explanation: The left lung typically has superior and inferior lobes divided by an oblique fissure.

questions.prompt: The indentation in the left lung accommodating the heart is the cardiac _____.
questions.hint: Found on the anterior border of the left lung.
questions.explanation: The cardiac notch makes room for the heart.

questions.prompt: The serous membrane covering lung tissue directly is the _____ pleura.
questions.hint: The opposite layer lines the thoracic wall.
questions.explanation: Visceral pleura is continuous with parietal pleura at the lung root.

questions.prompt: The region of entry for vessels, nerves, and bronchi on the medial lung is the _____.
questions.hint: It is the lung's root gateway.
questions.explanation: The lung hilum conveys bronchi and vascular/nerve structures.

questions.prompt: The alveolar epithelial cells covering most of the respiratory surface are type _____ pneumocytes.
questions.hint: The very thin gas-diffusion cells.
questions.explanation: Type I cells form the main simple squamous surface.

questions.prompt: Surfactant is produced by type _____ pneumocytes.
questions.hint: These are also called septal cells.
questions.explanation: Type II cells produce surfactant and support epithelial repair.

questions.prompt: The mixture lowering alveolar fluid surface tension is pulmonary _____.
questions.hint: Deficiency can cause alveolar instability.
questions.explanation: Surfactant reduces the work of inflation and limits collapse.

questions.prompt: The phagocytic dust cells in the alveoli are alveolar _____.
questions.hint: They engulf airborne debris.
questions.explanation: Macrophages provide local immune surveillance.

questions.prompt: The thin barrier composed of alveolar epithelium, basal laminae, and capillary endothelium is the respiratory _____.
questions.hint: A critical diffusion interface.
questions.explanation: The respiratory membrane makes exchange possible across a short distance.

questions.prompt: The inverse pressure–volume relation at constant gas temperature is _____ law.
questions.hint: Smaller volume means greater pressure for a fixed gas amount.
questions.explanation: Boyle's law explains pressure changes when thoracic volume changes.

questions.prompt: During inhalation the diaphragm _____, flattening and descending.
questions.hint: The active inspiration phase.
questions.explanation: Contraction expands the thoracic cavity and helps lower alveolar pressure.

questions.prompt: Normal quiet exhalation mainly uses passive elastic _____.
questions.hint: The lungs spring back toward a smaller volume.
questions.explanation: Recoil raises alveolar pressure and pushes air outward.

questions.prompt: The primary rib-elevating inspiratory muscles are the _____ intercostals.
questions.hint: Paired with the diaphragm in the lecture.
questions.explanation: External intercostal muscles elevate ribs in inspiration.

questions.prompt: If lung pressure is _____ than atmospheric pressure, air flows into the lungs.
questions.hint: Think of movement down a pressure gradient.
questions.explanation: Inspiration follows an alveolar pressure drop below outside pressure.

questions.prompt: The resting air volume entering or leaving with a typical breath is _____ volume.
questions.hint: This is abbreviated TV or VT.
questions.explanation: Tidal volume describes one ordinary breath.

questions.prompt: The air left after a maximal forced exhalation is _____ volume.
questions.hint: It is not removable by normal spirometry.
questions.explanation: Residual air remains even after forceful expiration.

questions.prompt: The extra air inhalable above a normal breath is inspiratory _____ volume.
questions.hint: It is not included in the normal tidal breath.
questions.explanation: IRV measures further inspiratory capacity beyond an ordinary breath.

questions.prompt: Vital capacity is tidal volume plus inspiratory reserve volume plus _____ reserve volume.
questions.hint: The additional air expelled after ordinary expiration.
questions.explanation: VC = TV + IRV + ERV.

questions.prompt: Total lung capacity equals vital capacity plus _____ volume.
questions.hint: The air that cannot be fully exhaled.
questions.explanation: TLC includes RV beyond vital capacity.

questions.prompt: The pressure contributed by a single gas in a mixture is its _____ pressure.
questions.hint: The P in PO₂ and PCO₂.
questions.explanation: Diffusion is driven by partial-pressure gradients.

questions.prompt: The relationship between gas partial pressure and dissolved gas concentration at fixed temperature is _____ law.
questions.hint: Think of a carbonated drink releasing CO₂ when opened.
questions.explanation: Henry's law describes gas dissolution at given temperature.

questions.prompt: Net oxygen diffusion in the lungs occurs from alveoli toward pulmonary _____.
questions.hint: The incoming blood has lower PO₂ than alveolar air.
questions.explanation: O₂ moves down its partial-pressure gradient into blood.

questions.prompt: At tissues, carbon dioxide ordinarily diffuses from cells into systemic _____.
questions.hint: Active cells produce metabolic CO₂.
questions.explanation: Tissue PCO₂ drives CO₂ transfer into nearby blood.

questions.prompt: Hemoglobin carrying oxygen is called _____.
questions.hint: It has O₂ bound to heme sites.
questions.explanation: Oxyhemoglobin predominates when PO₂ favors loading.

questions.prompt: The S-shaped oxygen–hemoglobin binding curve is partly explained by _____ binding.
questions.hint: Binding one O₂ changes the next binding step.
questions.explanation: Hemoglobin subunits influence each other's O₂ affinity.

questions.prompt: The effect by which increased CO₂ and H⁺ favor oxygen unloading is the _____ effect.
questions.hint: Named for a physiologist.
questions.explanation: The Bohr effect helps direct oxygen to metabolically active tissue.

questions.prompt: The PO₂-dependent fraction of hemoglobin's oxygen-binding sites occupied is its oxygen _____.
questions.hint: Often presented as a percent.
questions.explanation: Hb saturation varies along the oxygen dissociation curve.

questions.prompt: The main blood-borne form of carbon dioxide-derived carbon is _____.
questions.hint: It is not mainly free carbonic acid.
questions.explanation: About 70% of CO₂ equivalents are transported through the bicarbonate pathway.

questions.prompt: The enzyme that rapidly catalyzes reversible CO₂ hydration in RBCs is carbonic _____.
questions.hint: It is abundant in red blood cells.
questions.explanation: Carbonic anhydrase speeds CO₂/H₂CO₃ interconversion.

questions.prompt: The red-cell membrane exchange of chloride for bicarbonate is the _____ shift.
questions.hint: Bicarbonate leaves RBCs as chloride enters systemic blood.
questions.explanation: This exchange helps carry CO₂ equivalents to the lungs.

questions.prompt: CO₂ chemically bound to hemoglobin's globin chains forms _____.
questions.hint: Not oxyhemoglobin.
questions.explanation: This form represents part of blood CO₂ transport.

questions.prompt: Retention of excess carbon dioxide tends to produce respiratory _____.
questions.hint: Extra CO₂ often increases H⁺.
questions.explanation: CO₂ accumulation can lower arterial pH.

questions.prompt: The key brainstem region containing the respiratory groups DRG and VRG is the medulla _____.
questions.hint: Lower part of the brainstem.
questions.explanation: Medullary networks generate and organize breathing activity.

questions.prompt: In the lecture's older terminology, the pontine center that inhibits prolonged inspiration is the _____ center.
questions.hint: This is the inspiratory-limiting pontine label.
questions.explanation: Pneumotaxic influence helps shape inspiratory termination.

questions.prompt: The center described as facilitating sustained inspiration is the _____ center.
questions.hint: Paired with pneumotaxic in older diagrams.
questions.explanation: Apneustic is a historical descriptor of inspiratory-facilitating pontine circuitry.

questions.prompt: Elevated arterial CO₂ affects central chemoreceptors largely through changes in _____ pH.
questions.hint: Consider the fluid bathing brainstem chemosensitive neurons.
questions.explanation: CO₂ shifts local pH and elicits ventilation feedback.

questions.prompt: The main motor nerve of the diaphragm is the _____ nerve.
questions.hint: It arises chiefly from C3–C5.
questions.explanation: Phrenic motor output drives diaphragm contraction.

questions.prompt: Low oxygen availability in body tissues is called _____.
questions.hint: Distinguish this from high CO₂.
questions.explanation: Hypoxia is tissue oxygen deficiency.

questions.prompt: Inflammation of the larynx affecting voice is _____.
questions.hint: A common cause of hoarseness.
questions.explanation: Inflamed vocal folds vibrate abnormally.

questions.prompt: Infection or inflammation filling alveoli with fluid can result in _____.
questions.hint: A lung infection impairing exchange surfaces.
questions.explanation: Pneumonia commonly causes alveolar inflammation and exudate.

questions.prompt: A disease associated with thick airway mucus because of CFTR dysfunction is _____.
questions.hint: Hereditary epithelial ion-transport defect.
questions.explanation: Thick secretions impair mucociliary clearance.

questions.prompt: A condition with reversible bronchoconstriction and airway inflammation is _____.
questions.hint: Often causes wheeze.
questions.explanation: Asthma produces variable airflow obstruction.
